PullRequest.Title: Fix Markdown editor gutter markers for pure additions
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary
Fix missing rich Markdown editor gutter markers for pure insertions.

Keep all changed line ranges for editor gutters, and apply the deletion/modification-only filter specifically when producing classic preview indicators. This preserves existing preview behavior while allowing the rich editor to show added-line markers.

Add provider-to-marker regression coverage for insertions at the start and middle, appended sections, CRLF line endings, deletions, modifications, and unchanged content.

## Scope
Follow-up to merged #340505. This PR contains only the additional gutter fix, cherry-picked onto current main; none of the already-merged adoption commits are repeated.

## Validation
`scripts\test-integration.bat --suite markdown --grep "Markdown editor diff"`

**8 tests passed.**

The extracted commit's stable patch ID matches the original local commit `5798e2db661`.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or edit an inline rich Markdown document diff containing pure additions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the webview is ready, the document-diff listener awaits the version-cached text diff, converts every changed hunk to source offsets, and sends one gutter-marker notification before the new markers appear.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: vscode.workspace.getTextDiff computes/streams the original-to-modified text diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold computation per original/modified document-version pair; all getters for the same pair reuse the cached promise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same text-diff boundary ran with the same options and frequency; pure-addition changes were consumed for added-line mappings but omitted from changedLineRanges.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The diff must complete before gutter markers can be produced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: A gutterMarkers notification serializes markers to the Markdown editor webview.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One notification per ready/current document-change publish; marker payload is one entry per effective diff hunk, including pure-addition hunks after this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The notification already occurred, but a pure-addition-only diff carried an empty marker array; this PR adds the intended O(H) marker payload for H addition hunks without increasing notification count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The notification and webview model update are required for gutter markers to become visible, but do not block document editing.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with document line count in the existing diff and with effective diff-hunk count H for the newly included marker objects, not with every added line (contiguous additions form one hunk).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each document-change event can start an asynchronous publish; identical document versions share the provider's cached promise, while newer versions may overlap and stale results are discarded. The PR does not change this scheduling or add calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold document-version pairs invoke getTextDiff once. Repeated requests for unchanged versions reuse #cachedLineChanges, including concurrent callers; changing either document version replaces the cache. There is no persistent cross-version retention or negative-cache state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the added O(H) allocation/serialization and unchanged one-call boundary cardinality from the traced provider, cache, RPC, and webview consumer.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very fragmented generated Markdown could produce many addition hunks, but each newly transmitted marker is a small fixed-shape object and this is the required feature output; no evidence shows material latency, rendering, or memory regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The bounded per-hunk work directly implements the requested gutter markers, while diff frequency, IPC count, stale-result handling, and cache lifecycle are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render inline or side-by-side classic Markdown previews after document changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Preview refresh requests line changes and mappings; on a cold version pair it awaits the text diff, then computes preview indicators and line mappings used to render/synchronize the preview.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: vscode.workspace.getTextDiff computes/streams the line and inner changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold operation per document-version pair per diff provider; modified changes and mapping getters share it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same operation already ran and produced the same added/deleted/mapping data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Preview line-change metadata and side-by-side mappings wait for this result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing preview refresh sends rendered preview state and line-change metadata to its webview.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing refresh per preview update; pure-addition line metadata was already represented by the added-line list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Pure additions already populated added lines, while preview changeIndicators excluded them; this remains unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Preview rendering waits on the existing refresh path; the PR does not enlarge its returned preview payload because pure additions remain filtered out of changeIndicators.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The PR temporarily retains all H diff hunks and performs one O(H) filter before indicator splitting; downstream classic-preview indicators still include only deletion/modification hunks, and existing line/mapping work scales with changed lines/document size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The line-diff provider coalesces getters for the same version pair through one cached promise. Preview refresh behavior and concurrency are unchanged by the PR.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The first getter for a document-version pair computes all line changes; subsequent preview and mapping getters reuse the promise until either document version changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from direct inspection that preview outputs and expensive boundary cardinality are unchanged; only a bounded linear filter/allocation is added.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: H can be large for highly fragmented diffs, but the added temporary references and one linear filter are minor beside the already-required diff iteration and arrays, with no boundary or rendered-output amplification.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The additional O(H) temporary array/filter is bounded to each cold diff computation and preserves existing preview output without creating repeated boundary work or retained growth.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. Traced rich-editor gutter updates and classic preview diff consumers, including version caching, overlapping updates, text-diff and webview boundaries, payload cardinality, and model application. The PR adds only intended per-addition-hunk marker data plus a bounded filter; no high-confidence actionable performance issue or regression fix was found.
